Code: TRUTH_LOCK stores ctx.runHead from gitState.head. SELECT records selectionAtRunHead, which holds: selectedAt (the register's generatedAtHead), runHead, the committed and re-derived {decision, selected}, consistent, stale, executing, and ownerOverride (GO-ORD-1 or GO-ORD-2, recorded). EXECUTE's authorize step refuses STALE_SELECTION for the selected item before isolation and dispatch, unless an override applies.

Override exemption: appropriate, but broad. The objective itself says 'refuses (or records the owner override)'. GO-ORD-1 and GO-ORD-2 are evaluated against the RE-DERIVED run-head state: GO-ORD-1 needs the tiedSet to equal the current tie, and GO-ORD-2 needs a matching contractSha256 plus a one-shot claim. So the executed item comes from the run-head computation, and the override is recorded. The exemption keys on any applied owner record rather than on the specific stale difference. It weakens nothing that existed before, because before this change there was no refusal at all.

False-refusal risk is low. All 21 committed GO traces (H through P7) recorded consistentWithCommittedRegisterEvidence: true, so the guard would have refused none of them. CI checks the committed register against a fresh computation, and runtime/bin/odg-strategic-select.test.ts passes.

The guard fails open when there is no committed decisionRecord: consistent is null, so stale is false and nothing is refused. selectedAt is the register's generatedAtHead. That is always the parent of the PR that commits the register, so it differs from runHead by construction and is informational only; staleness is decided by content.

The tests prove the ACs but are thin. AC1 injects a stale committed record ('STALE-ITEM') into an authorized fixture: the trace shows stale true, dispatch is called 0 times, and EXECUTE shows STALE_SELECTION. AC2 checks that runHead is 'h' and consistent is true, but it only checks that the selectedAt KEY exists; in the fixture its value is null because SS.compute sets no generatedAtHead. No test covers the override path (stale plus an applied GO-ORD-1/2 record lets the run proceed and records ownerOverride). Recommended follow-up test.

recommit() keeps the fixtures self-consistent by recomputing the register over the edited contracts, which is how a real committed register behaves. It does not mask the guard: the AC1 fixture deliberately breaks that consistency.
